name: Hurghada
tagline: Egypt's original and largest Red Sea resort city, a long strip of beach hotels backed onto some of the coast's richest offshore reefs and wreck diving.
highlight: Cutting the engine over the Abu Nuhas wrecks, sunlight falling through impossibly clear water onto a century-old ship's hull.
shortDescription: Egypt's original and largest Red Sea resort city, built around long beach hotels, offshore reef and wreck diving, and easy day trips to Giftun Island and El Gouna.
metaDescription: A Hurghada travel guide: Giftun Island, the Abu Nuhas wrecks, dolphin-watching trips, El Gouna, food and how to plan a Red Sea resort holiday.
knownFor: Long beach resorts, offshore diving and snorkelling, Giftun Island

image.file: File:Beach of the Paradise Island of Hurghada.jpg
image.alt: The beach at Hurghada on Egypt's Red Sea coast

intro: Hurghada is genuinely Egypt's original Red Sea resort city, a long strip of beach hotels on the mainland coast that first put this stretch of coastline on the map.
Its appeal rests genuinely on easy access to exceptional offshore diving and snorkelling, from Giftun Island's reefs to the wrecks scattered across Abu Nuhas.
Most visitors genuinely split time between resort beach days and boat trips, with the more boutique lagoon town of El Gouna an easy day trip up the coast.

whyVisit.intro: Hurghada's case rests genuinely on being the most accessible, best-value base for Red Sea beach and diving holidays.

points.title: It's genuinely the most established Red Sea resort city
points.text: Decades of tourism infrastructure mean flights, hotels and dive centres for every budget.

points.title: The offshore diving is genuinely exceptional
points.text: Giftun Island's reefs and the Abu Nuhas wrecks rank among the Red Sea's best.

points.title: It's genuinely strong value for a Red Sea base
points.text: Generally more affordable than Sharm El Sheikh, with comparable water and diving quality.

points.title: El Gouna is genuinely a short, easy day trip
points.text: A more boutique lagoon town with its own beaches, restaurants and marina.

points.title: It works genuinely well for families
points.text: All-inclusive resorts, calm swimming beaches and organised excursions suit every age.

attractionsIntro: Hurghada's essential sights are genuinely spread between its beach resort strip and the reefs and islands offshore.

attractions.name: Hurghada's beach strip
attractions.text: Genuinely a long run of sandy beach hotels facing the Red Sea, the backbone of most visits here.
attractions.tip: Genuinely most resort beaches are private to guests, though public beach clubs exist nearby.

attractions.name: Giftun Island

image.alt: Giftun Island off the coast of Hurghada

attractions.text: Genuinely a protected island a short boat ride offshore, its fringing reefs among the best snorkelling near Hurghada.
attractions.tip: Genuinely book a full-day boat trip that includes multiple snorkel or dive stops.

attractions.name: Hurghada Marina
attractions.text: Genuinely the town's smartest stretch, lined with restaurants, cafés and yachts departing for reef trips.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a pleasant spot for an evening stroll and dinner by the water.

attractions.name: El Gouna

image.alt: The lagoon town of El Gouna near Hurghada

attractions.text: Genuinely a more boutique, design-conscious lagoon town twenty minutes up the coast, popular as a day trip or standalone stay.
attractions.tip: Genuinely rent a bike once there — El Gouna's lagoons and bridges are made for it.

attractions.name: Dolphin House (Shaab El Erg)

image.file: File:A pod of spinner dolphins in the Red Sea.jpg
image.alt: Spinner dolphins at Shaab El Erg near Hurghada

attractions.text: Genuinely a reef known for a resident pod of wild spinner dolphins, a real highlight for snorkellers on a good day.
attractions.tip: Genuinely choose an operator that keeps a respectful distance and never chases the pod.

attractions.name: The Abu Nuhas wrecks

image.file: File:Abu Nuhas parts of Kimon M.JPG
image.alt: A shipwreck at Abu Nuhas near Hurghada

attractions.text: Genuinely known among divers as the Red Sea's 'Ships' Graveyard', a reef scattered with several historic wrecks.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a trip best suited to certified divers with some wreck diving experience.

attractions.name: Sakkala and El Dahar
attractions.text: Genuinely Hurghada's older, more local quarters, with a working market, mosque and a far less touristy feel than the resort strip.
attractions.tip: Genuinely worth a taxi over for an authentic meal away from the hotels.

thingsToDoIntro: Hurghada genuinely centres on the water, with boat trips to reefs, wrecks and islands filling most itineraries.

thingsToDo.title: Snorkel or dive Giftun Island

image.alt: A boat trip to Giftun Island near Hurghada

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely classic Hurghada day out, boating to the island's reefs for snorkelling or diving.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely choose a smaller boat trip over a large day-cruise for a better experience in the water.

thingsToDo.title: Dive the wrecks at Abu Nuhas

image.alt: Diving the wrecks at Abu Nuhas

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely bucket-list trip for certified divers, exploring several historic shipwrecks in one reef system.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book through a dive centre experienced with the site's currents and depths.

thingsToDo.title: Take a boat trip to see wild dolphins

image.file: File:A spinner dolphin in the Red Sea.jpg

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely memorable excursion out to Shaab El Erg's resident spinner dolphin pod.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely go with an operator that limits group size and respects the dolphins' space.

thingsToDo.title: Ride a glass-bottom boat

image.file: File:Gelbes Schiff mit Glasboden im Roten Meer in Ägypten 2H1A6659WI.jpg
image.alt: A glass-bottom boat on the Red Sea near Hurghada

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely easy way to see the reef for non-swimmers or anyone travelling with young children.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely widely offered from the marina and resort tour desks.

thingsToDo.title: Go on a desert safari by quad bike
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely popular half-day break from the water, riding out into the desert with a Bedouin camp stop.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely afternoon or sunset departures avoid the hottest part of the day.

thingsToDo.title: Day-trip to El Gouna
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely worthwhile change of pace, exploring El Gouna's lagoons, marina and beach clubs by bike or taxi.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely easy to arrange independently — no need for an organised tour.

foodIntro: Hurghada's food genuinely spans resort international dining alongside fresh Red Sea seafood and Egyptian staples.

foods.name: Fresh Red Sea seafood
foods.text: Genuinely a highlight of dining here, fish and shellfish landed fresh from the surrounding waters.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants around the marina and throughout the resort strip.

foods.name: Grilled kofta

image.alt: Grilled kofta, spiced minced meat skewers

foods.text: A genuinely reliable classic, found throughout the town's restaurants.

foods.name: Koshari

image.alt: Koshari, Egypt's national dish of rice, lentils and pasta

foods.text: Genuinely available at Egyptian restaurants away from the resort strip, a taste of home for local staff and visitors alike.
foods.whereToTry: Local restaurants around Sakkala and El Dahar.

foods.name: Ful medames

image.alt: Ful medames, a traditional Egyptian fava bean breakfast

foods.text: A genuinely traditional breakfast option, found at both resort buffets and local cafés.
foods.whereToTry: Cafés and resort breakfasts throughout Hurghada.

foods.name: Taameya (Egyptian falafel)
foods.text: Genuinely Egypt's own fava bean version of falafel, available throughout the town.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants and street stalls throughout Hurghada.

foods.name: Karkade (hibiscus tea)
foods.text: Genuinely a refreshing national drink, a nice complement to a day on the water.
foods.whereToTry: Cafés and restaurants throughout the resort area.

accommodation.intro: Hurghada genuinely offers Egypt's widest range of Red Sea resort accommodation, from budget hotels to luxury all-inclusive properties.

areas.name: The Marina and Sekalla
areas.bestFor: Being genuinely central, with the widest choice of restaurants and nightlife
areas.text: A lively, convenient base within easy reach of boat trips and dining.

areas.name: El Gouna
areas.bestFor: A genuinely quieter, more boutique alternative base
areas.text: Twenty minutes up the coast, with its own lagoons, beaches and marina.

gettingThere.intro: Hurghada is genuinely well connected by direct flights, both domestic and international.

options.text: Genuinely the standard domestic connection, taking about an hour.
options.detail: Frequent daily flights make Hurghada an easy Red Sea addition to a Nile-focused trip.

options.text: Genuinely available from many European cities, especially in high season.
options.detail: A popular direct resort destination not requiring a Cairo stopover.

options.text: Genuinely a longer but budget-friendly overland option.
options.detail: Takes around six hours from Cairo, or roughly four from Luxor.

gettingAround.intro: Hurghada is genuinely spread along a long resort strip, with taxis and organised transfers the standard way around.

options.text: Genuinely the standard way to reach boat trips and excursions from your hotel.
options.detail: Most tour operators include hotel pickup as part of the trip.

options.text: Genuinely useful for reaching the marina, restaurants or El Gouna.
options.detail: Widely available, though agree the fare before starting your journey.

options.mode: On foot within your resort area
options.text: Genuinely easy within a single stretch of the strip.
options.detail: Covering the full length of Hurghada on foot is impractical given its size.

bestTime.headline: March to May and September to November for the most comfortable conditions
bestTime.summary: Hurghada is genuinely a year-round destination, with water temperatures staying warm even in winter.

seasons.text: Genuinely the most comfortable air and water temperatures for diving and beach time.
Genuinely very hot on land, though the water itself stays excellent for diving and snorkelling.
Genuinely mild and popular with visitors escaping colder climates, water temperatures still comfortable.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly — Hurghada's genuinely warm Red Sea waters make it a workable destination in any season.

itinerary.title: Three days in Hurghada
itinerary.intro: Built around a Giftun Island boat trip, a wreck dive or desert safari, and a day trip to El Gouna.

days.title: Giftun Island
days.summary: A full-day snorkelling or diving boat trip.
days.morning: Boat out to Giftun Island's reefs.
days.afternoon: Snorkelling or diving stops around the island.

days.title: Wrecks or desert
days.summary: A day for more advanced diving or a desert safari.
days.morning: Dive the wrecks at Abu Nuhas, if certified, or join a desert safari.
days.afternoon: Continue the boat trip or safari.

days.title: El Gouna
days.summary: A day trip up the coast.
days.afternoon: Explore El Gouna's lagoons, beaches and marina.
days.evening: Return to Hurghada for a final dinner.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Hurghada visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book genuinely with a reputable dive centre for any wreck or reef diving.
Bring genuinely your own certification card if you're a qualified diver.
Pack genuinely reef-safe sunscreen to help protect the coral.
Agree genuinely a price before any independently arranged desert safari or taxi.
Stay genuinely hydrated and use sun protection, even on boat trips.
Consider genuinely a half-board or all-inclusive resort — independent dining options are more spread out than in Sharm El Sheikh.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Hurghada?
faq.a: Four to six days genuinely allows for a proper mix of beach time, diving trips and a day trip to El Gouna.

faq.q: How does Hurghada compare to Sharm El Sheikh?
faq.a: Genuinely more affordable and less polished, with excellent offshore reefs and wreck diving rather than Sharm's dramatic drop-offs.
Yes, genuinely — all-inclusive resorts and calm beaches make it one of Egypt's most family-friendly bases.

faq.q: Do you need to be a certified diver to visit?
faq.a: No, genuinely not — excellent snorkelling and beginner dive courses are widely available.

faq.q: Can beginners dive the wrecks at Abu Nuhas?
faq.a: Some genuinely shallower sections are accessible to newer divers, though the deeper wrecks suit more experienced divers.

faq.q: Can you combine Hurghada with the Nile Valley?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely easily — a direct flight connects to Luxor or Cairo, making it a natural Red Sea extension to a Nile-focused Egypt trip.
